Command: Do Not Plow with Ox and Donkey Together
Summary: Thou shalt not plow with an ox and an ass together. The third of the kilayim mixture laws — the team, not the seed or the garment.
Commandment: Do not plow with an ox and a donkey yoked together.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The traditional reading also notes a practical wisdom — two unlike animals pull unevenly and the weaker suffers — but Scripture states no reason, so that reading is labeled traditional, not scriptural. It is not a New Testament obligation.
Purpose: TRADITIONAL reading: unlike animals yoked together pull unevenly, to the suffering of the weaker; the law guards both order and mercy to animals. Scripture states the prohibition without a reason (Deuteronomy 22:10).
